T1158.long: To prevent normal users from accidentally changing special files on a system, most operating systems have the concept of a ‘hidden’ file. These files don’t show up when a user browses the file system with a GUI or when using normal commands on the command line. Users must explicitly ask to show the hidden files either via a series of Graphical User Interface (GUI) prompts or with command line switches (dir /a for Windows and ls –a for Linux and macOS).

\par by the NATO Secretary General following a meeting of the NATO-Russia Council}{\rtlch\fcs1 \af0\afs28 \ltrch\fcs0 \b\f0\fs28\insrsid2187550\charrsid221283
\par I have just chaired a meeting of the NATO-Russia Council.
\par We had a frank and substantial discussion on issues of importance to our common security.
\par In times of tension, dialogue is more important than ever. So we remain committed to dialogue. And we will continue to keep channels of communication open.
first topic we discussed was the crisis in and around Ukraine.
\par Allies and Russia have profound disagreements on the crisis.
\par Today, Allies reiterated their strong support for Ukraine\rquote s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
\par Allies do not, and will not, recognise Russia\rquote s illegal and illegitimate annexation of Crimea.
\par The situation in eastern Ukraine also remains of deep concern.
\par Ceasefire violations have reached record levels in recent months. Heavy weapons have not been withdrawn. And OSCE monitors have repeatedly become targets.

\par The Minsk Agreements provide a plan for the settlement of the conflict in eastern Ukraine. All signatories should fully comply with their commitments. And Allies called on Russia to use its considerable influence on the militants
to meet their commitments in full.
We also discussed the security situation in Afghanistan, including the regional terrorist threat.
\par Supporting Afghan forces to provide for their country\rquote s security remains crucial. That is what NATO and our partners are doing. With training and funding.
\par Because a stable Afghanistan is in everyone\rquote s interest. So all outside actors need to play a constructive role in supporting the National Unity Government to stabilise Afghanistan.
y activities, transparency and risk reduction.
\par Behaving responsibly and predictably reduces the risk of misunderstanding, miscalculation, and unintended escalation.
\par As a result of our discussion at the NATO-Russia Council in July, we had briefings by repre
sentatives of the Baltic Sea Project Team and the International Civil Aviation Organization. Their work has made an important contribution towards improving air safety over the Baltic Sea.
\par I welcome Finland\rquote s initiative to host a technical-level meeting to take this work forward in the new year, supported by the International Civil Aviation Organization.
\par The meeting will review the implementation of the recommendations made by the Baltic Sea Project Team. And it will assess whether any further work needs to be done.
\par It is important that we all follow the rules that are already there. Behave responsibly and safely. And engage in good airmanship at all times.
\par Russia also gave us a briefing on the recent KAVKAZ-2016 exercise. And NATO gave a presentation on Exercise Trident Juncture 2016.

\par Transparency on military exercises is essential. In the OSCE, 57 nations \endash  including all NATO Allies and Russia \endash  have agreed on rules governing military activities in Europe. Including the observation and notification of exercises.

\par Today, Allies raised particular concern over the excessive use of snap exercises. These are destabilising, and do not improve the overall climate of our relations.Many around the table called for the members of the NATO-Russia Council to contribut
e at the OSCE to updating the Vienna Document on military exercises and activities.
So this was the third time the NATO-Russia Council has met this year.Allies and Russia hold different views. And our meeting does not indicate a return to business as usual.
\par But without talking, we cannot solve our differences and improve mutual understanding.

\par NATO does not seek confrontation and poses no threat. Everything we do \endash  including strengthening our presence in the east of the Alliance \endash  is defensive, proportionate and in line with our international commitments.
\par NATO's goal is, and remains, to protect our allies, prevent conflict and preserve the peace.
